blocks.orig: If you are looking for a beautiful African country to visit for a luxury vacation, then look no further than Tanzania. Read further about the best tourist attractions in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Searching for a beautiful African country where you can spend a luxury holiday? Tanzania is the answer. Below you can read about the finest tourist attractions in Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Tanzania is packed with natural beauty and the opportunity to experience wildlife in a way that you can nowhere else in the world.
blocks.html: Natural beauty is everywhere in Tanzania, and the chance to see wildlife here is unlike anything you will find anywhere else on earth.

blocks.orig: Tanzania really is a once in a lifetime holiday destination. So, if you are thinking of visiting, it is likely that you will want to fit in as many tourist attractions as possible during your trip. If so, you are in the right place.
blocks.html: A trip to Tanzania truly is a once in a lifetime holiday. If you are considering a visit, chances are you will want to squeeze as many tourist attractions as you can into your stay. If that sounds like you, you have come to the right place.

blocks.orig: In this guide, we’ll take a look at 20 of the best tourist attractions in Tanzania to help you plan for your luxury vacation. So, if you want to find out more, keep on reading!
blocks.html: This guide walks you through 20 of the best tourist attractions Tanzania has to offer, so you can plan your luxury holiday with confidence. Want to know more? Then read on!

blocks.orig: First up, it goes without saying that you have to travel to the Serengeti during your trip to Tanzania. Just like Mount Kilimanjaro, the Serengeti is one of the biggest tourist attractions of Tanzania, and it is perfect for any animal lover.
blocks.html: To begin with, it almost goes without saying: a trip to Tanzania has to include the Serengeti. Together with Mount Kilimanjaro, the Serengeti ranks among the biggest tourist attractions in Tanzania, and anyone who loves animals will feel at home here.

blocks.orig: These vast plains are home to millions of wildlife, and animals passing through. It is home to the Big Five, and a very popular location for game drives.
blocks.html: Millions of animals live on or pass through these enormous plains. The Big Five are found here, and the area is a very popular spot for game drives.

blocks.orig: It is also the second-largest national park in Tanzania, and the location of the great wildebeest migration every year. Many people visit Tanzania purely to go on a safari to the Serengeti.
blocks.html: Only one park in the country is bigger, and this is where the famous wildebeest herds make their great trek every year. For plenty of travellers, a safari here is the sole purpose of their journey to Tanzania.

blocks.orig: If you want to go to an area where you can see both immense natural beauty, and lots of wildlife, then you should head to Ngorongoro Conservation Area. This area is home to thousands of animals, including some of the Big Five.
blocks.html: Looking for a place where immense natural beauty and plenty of wildlife come together? Then the Ngorongoro Conservation Area is where you should go. Thousands of animals live here, among them several of the Big Five.

blocks.orig: Ngorongoro Conservation Area literally combines both nature and wildlife. This is because the biggest geographical draw to this area is the Ngorongoro Crater.
blocks.html: In the Ngorongoro Conservation Area nature and wildlife are quite literally combined. The reason is that the main geographical attraction of the area is the Ngorongoro Crater itself.

blocks.orig: However, this crater is also home to all the thousands of wildlife that we mentioned earlier. It really is a tourist attraction in Tanzania you don’t want to miss!
blocks.html: At the same time, that crater is where all those thousands of animals we mentioned above actually live. This is one tourist attraction in Tanzania you really should not skip!

blocks.orig: Another great national park to visit for wildlife is Tarangire National Park.
blocks.html: For more animal encounters, Tarangire National Park is another superb choice.

blocks.orig: This National Park is perfect for people who aren’t overly interested in seeing the big five, and are instead happy to see more-relaxed animals in their natural habitat.
blocks.html: This park suits travellers who are not especially focused on ticking off the Big Five, and who would rather watch more laid-back animals going about their lives in their natural surroundings.

blocks.orig: It is world famous for its baobab trees that are enormous with unique shapes that are magnificent to look at.
blocks.html: The park is known across the world for its baobab trees: huge, strangely shaped and wonderful to look at.

blocks.orig: Tarangire is the national park to go to if you want to spend a significant amount of your vacation bird-watching.
blocks.html: If you plan to spend a good part of your holiday bird-watching, Tarangire is the national park to choose.

blocks.orig: It is also great if you are interested in migratory wildlife, such as buffalo, zebra, wildebeest, and elephants as all these animals live in the National Park.
blocks.html: It is equally rewarding if migratory wildlife interests you, because buffalo, zebra, wildebeest and elephants all live within the park.

blocks.orig: Tarangire actually has the highest concentration of elephants in the world, so if you want to see elephants, this is the place for you!
blocks.html: In fact, Tarangire has the highest concentration of elephants anywhere in the world, so if elephants are what you are after, this is where to go!

blocks.orig: As you have probably noticed, quite a lot of the tourist attractions in this guide are national parks.
blocks.html: By now it will be clear that national parks make up a large share of this list.

blocks.orig: Tanzania isn’t a country that you visit to spend your time indoors, instead it is somewhere that you visit to immerse yourself in nature. One of the best places to do this is Lake Manyara National park.
blocks.html: Tanzania is not a country you visit to sit indoors; you come here to surround yourself with nature. Lake Manyara National park is one of the best places to do exactly that.

blocks.orig: This national park is incredibly diverse, with areas of grasslands, swamps, woodlands, and forests. A large amount of the national park is composed of water, so it is the place to go if you love birds.
blocks.html: The park is remarkably varied, with grasslands, swamps, woodlands and forests. Because a large share of the park is made up of water, it is the place to be if birds are your passion.

blocks.orig: It is also home to the largest concentration of baboons on the planet, so if you want to see these beautiful creatures, consider a trip to Lake Manyara.
blocks.html: Lake Manyara also has the largest concentration of baboons on earth, so if you would like to watch these beautiful animals, think about including a visit.

blocks.orig: Another huge attraction in Tanzania is Mount Kilimanjaro. For many people, Mount Kilimanjaro is the main reason why they visit Tanzania.
blocks.html: Yet another major attraction in Tanzania is Mount Kilimanjaro. For a lot of people, the mountain is the main reason they come to Tanzania in the first place.

blocks.orig: If you are somebody who loves climbing and hiking, climbing Kilimanjaro is the ultimate challenge, and it is something that many people spend years training for.
blocks.html: If climbing and hiking are your thing, climbing Kilimanjaro is the ultimate challenge, and plenty of people train for years to take it on.

blocks.orig: Mount Kilimanjaro definitely isn’t a tourist attraction for the faint-hearted, and it isn’t one that you can do on a whim either.
blocks.html: Mount Kilimanjaro is certainly not an attraction for the faint-hearted, nor is it something you can decide to do on a whim.

blocks.orig: But with planning and preparation, you should definitely consider fitting this into your Tanzania vacation.
blocks.html: With proper planning and preparation, though, it is well worth considering as part of your Tanzania holiday.

blocks.orig: Zanzibar is famous for its crystal clear waters and sparkling white beaches, so we won’t say too much about them.
blocks.html: The crystal clear water and sparkling white sand of Zanzibar are famous already, so we will keep this short.

blocks.orig: But what we will say is that you shouldn’t make a trip to Tanzania without fitting in a trip to at least one of these beaches. If you do, you will live to regret it!
blocks.html: What we will say is this: do not leave Tanzania without visiting at least one of these beaches. Skip them and you will regret it later!

blocks.orig: Some of the best beaches in Zanzibar to visit are Paje, Jambiani, Kendwa and Nungwi, so these are excellent areas to explore during your trip.
blocks.html: Paje, Jambiani, Kendwa and Nungwi are four of the island's finest stretches of sand, and each is a wonderful base from which to explore.

blocks.orig: On the topic of Zanzibar, we have to mention Stone Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and it is easy to see why. It is totally unique, and very different to all the other attractions in this list. We definitely recommend giving it a visit!
blocks.html: Staying with Zanzibar, Stone Town deserves a mention. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and it is not hard to see why: it is completely unique and quite unlike anything else in this list. We certainly recommend a visit!

blocks.orig: While you’re there, you might also want to pay Changuu Island (a.k.a. Prison Island) a visit to really immerse yourself in this country’s history.
blocks.html: While you are in the area, Changuu Island (also known as Prison Island) is worth a visit too if you want to get a deeper feel for the country's history.

blocks.orig: Julius Nyerere National park was formerly known as Selous Game Reserve and it was the largest game reserve in Africa, and it covers around 5% of Tanzania’s land mass.
blocks.html: Before it was renamed Julius Nyerere National park, this area went by the name Selous Game Reserve. At the time it was the largest game reserve on the African continent, and it takes up roughly 5% of the country's total surface.

blocks.orig: It had been a game reserve since the 1920s, and to this day there are still forbidden areas of the reserve where humans cannot go. Of course, it is now a National Park rather than a game reserve.
blocks.html: The area has been a game reserve since the 1920s, and even now there are parts of it that remain off limits to humans. Today, of course, it is a National Park rather than a game reserve.

blocks.orig: Julius Nyerere National Park is home to more than 350 recorded species, and it is truly beautiful. It is definitely worth spending a day exploring this area during your vacation.
blocks.html: More than 350 recorded species live in Julius Nyerere National Park, and the landscape is truly beautiful. Setting aside a day of your holiday to explore it is well worth it.

blocks.orig: Ruaha National Park was the largest national park in Tanzania, until Selous Game Reserve became Julius Nyerere National Park.
blocks.html: Before Selous was upgraded to become Julius Nyerere National Park, the title of Tanzania's biggest national park belonged to Ruaha.

blocks.orig: It is an area of immense natural beauty, and it has outstanding viewing platforms where you can observe wildlife in their natural habitat.
blocks.html: The scenery here is stunning, and there are superb lookout points from which you can observe animals going about their lives undisturbed.

blocks.orig: Ruaha National Park is one of the most difficult National Parks in Tanzania to access, but this only adds to its beauty.
blocks.html: Ruaha is among the hardest National Parks in Tanzania to reach, but that remoteness only adds to its charm.

blocks.orig: Tourist visits are possible if you go with a guide that knows the way, and this is often a good idea because Ruaha National Park is in a very remote area.
blocks.html: Visiting as a tourist is possible with a guide who knows the way, and that is usually a sensible choice given how remote Ruaha National Park is.

blocks.orig: Tanzania really is jam packed with National Parks, and another one that attracts many tourists to Tanzania is Mikumi.
blocks.html: Tanzania really is full of National Parks, and Mikumi is another one that draws many visitors to the country.

blocks.orig: There are lots of different animals that reside in Mikumi, including zebras, buffalo, elephants and more.
blocks.html: Many different animals make their home in Mikumi, among them zebras, buffalo, elephants and more.

blocks.orig: Of all the different National Parks in Tanzania, Mikumi is the best place to go for lions. Specifically, tree-climbing lions as the chances of you seeing tree climbing lions in this National Park are the highest in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Of all the National Parks in Tanzania, Mikumi is the best one for lions. Tree-climbing lions in particular: nowhere in Tanzania are your chances of spotting lions up a tree higher than here.

blocks.orig: If you are interested in chimpanzees, then you will likely be familiar with Gombe Stream National Park.
blocks.html: Anyone with an interest in chimpanzees will probably have heard of Gombe Stream National Park.

blocks.orig: This national park is most commonly associated with British conservationist Jane Goodall, and the work that she did here with chimpanzees.
blocks.html: The park is best known for its association with British conservationist Jane Goodall and the chimpanzee research she carried out here.

blocks.orig: If you want to see chimps in their natural habitat, then this is the national park to go to.
blocks.html: For chimps in their natural habitat, this is the national park to visit.

blocks.orig: It is a little off the beaten track, but you can immerse yourself in nature in a guided-tour of this area, and hopefully see some chimpanzees on the way.
blocks.html: Getting there takes a little effort, but a guided walk through the forest lets you soak up the surroundings and, with a bit of luck, meet a few chimpanzees along the route.

blocks.orig: Many people consider Mafia Island to be a step back in time. Even when Tanzania was becoming a tourist destination, Mafia Island remained untouched, and this is why it is still so beautiful today.
blocks.html: Visiting Mafia Island feels, to many, like travelling into the past. Tourism grew elsewhere in the country, but this island was left alone, and that is precisely why it remains so lovely today.

blocks.orig: If you enjoy diving or snorkeling, you have to go to Mafia Island during your vacation. It is packed with lots of different varieties of fish and coral gardens too.
blocks.html: If diving or snorkelling appeals to you, Mafia Island is a must during your holiday. The waters are full of many kinds of fish, and there are coral gardens as well.

blocks.orig: Perfect for anybody who enjoys spending time exploring the water. Mafia Island also has a whale shark season, so it is a great place to go diving with whale sharks if this is something that you are interested in.
blocks.html: It is ideal for anyone who likes to spend their time in and around the water. Mafia Island also has a whale shark season, so if diving with whale sharks is on your list, this is a great place to do it.

blocks.orig: The Beaches of Zanzibar are some of the most beautiful in the world, but if you want to see blue seas and sandy beaches, Pemba Island is definitely worth a visit!
blocks.html: Zanzibar's beaches rank among the most beautiful in the world, but for blue seas and sandy shores Pemba Island certainly deserves a visit too!

blocks.orig: Not only is Pemba Island filled with beautiful water and beaches, but it is also the home of luscious green vegetation and clove plantations.
blocks.html: The island has far more than sea and sand to offer: lush greenery covers much of it, and clove plantations are part of the landscape.

blocks.orig: The water around Pemba Island is filled with coral reefs and a whole variety of different marine life.
blocks.html: Around Pemba Island, the sea is full of coral reefs and a wide range of marine life.

blocks.orig: So, on your journey over to Pemba Island, you will likely get to see all sorts of wildlife that you wouldn’t see if you stuck to mainland Tanzania.
blocks.html: So on the crossing to Pemba Island you are likely to spot all kinds of wildlife you would never see if you stayed on the Tanzanian mainland.

blocks.orig: A lot of the attractions that we have spoken about in this list have been natural attractions, but Dar es Salaam is a little different.
blocks.html: Nearly everything covered so far has been about nature, but Dar es Salaam offers something of a different kind.

blocks.orig: Dar is the biggest cities in Tanzania, and it is somewhere that you should definitely try to visit during your trip!
blocks.html: Dar is the biggest city in Tanzania, and we would certainly encourage you to work a visit into your trip!

blocks.orig: Dar itself is packed with different attractions, such as the Open Air Village Museum, and it is a great opportunity to explore a built-up city that is located in a country that is mainly associated with nature.
blocks.html: The city itself has plenty of attractions, including the Open Air Village Museum, and it offers a great chance to explore a built-up city in a country that most people associate with nature.

blocks.orig: You should definitely squeeze a visit to Dar into your Tanzania trip.
blocks.html: Make room for a visit to Dar in your Tanzania itinerary if you can.

blocks.orig: We couldn’t make this guide without mentioning Materuni Waterfalls. These waterfalls are actually located in the Kilimanjaro region of the country, so if you are planning on hiking this mountain, you could easily squeeze in a trip to these waterfalls.
blocks.html: A guide like this would not be complete without Materuni Waterfalls. The falls are found in the Kilimanjaro region, so if a hike up the mountain is part of your plans, a detour to see them is easy to arrange.

blocks.orig: As well as being able to see these beautiful waterfalls, you can also do a coffee tour of the area. So, if you love natural beauty, and you love coffee, this is the attraction for you!
blocks.html: Besides admiring the beautiful falls, you can also join a coffee tour in the area. If you love natural beauty and you love coffee, this attraction was made for you!

blocks.orig: Similar to Dar which we mentioned earlier, if you are interested in visiting cities during your trip to Tanzania, we would definitely recommend going to Mbeya.
blocks.html: Much like Dar, which we covered earlier, Mbeya is a city we would certainly recommend if urban visits are part of your Tanzania plans.

blocks.orig: Mbeya is a city in the Southwest of Tanzania and it is located at the base of Mbeya and Poroto Mountain Ranges.
blocks.html: Mbeya lies in the Southwest of Tanzania, at the foot of the Mbeya and Poroto Mountain Ranges.

blocks.orig: This city is the perfect place to experience man-made and natural beauty alongside one another, and it is very different to cities that you might visit in other countries.
blocks.html: Here man-made and natural beauty sit side by side, and the city feels very different from the ones you might visit in other countries.

blocks.orig: It is totally unique, thanks to its green lakes, exciting waterfalls, and the garden of God, and well worth visiting if you are in the area.
blocks.html: With its green lakes, dramatic waterfalls and the garden of God, Mbeya is completely unique and well worth a visit if you are nearby.

blocks.orig: A great National Park to visit if you are interested in encountering a range of different habitats is Udzungwa Mountains National Park.
blocks.html: If you would like to experience a whole range of habitats in one place, Udzungwa Mountains National Park is a great choice.

blocks.orig: In this single National Park, you will encounter rainforests, mountain forests, woodlands, grasslands and steppe too. So, it is well worth visiting if you want to immerse yourself in nature.
blocks.html: Within this one National Park you will find rainforest, mountain forest, woodland, grassland and steppe. For anyone who wants to be surrounded by nature, it is well worth the trip.

blocks.orig: Especially if you want to encounter a variety of different birds, and monkeys too!
blocks.html: That goes double if you are keen to see a wide variety of birds, and monkeys as well!

blocks.orig: If you want to explore the history of Tanzania, then we would recommend a visit to Bagamoyo. Bagamoyo is a historic coastal town that was founded in the 1700s, and it is truly beautiful.
blocks.html: For a look at Tanzania's history, we would suggest a visit to Bagamoyo. This historic coastal town was founded in the 1700s and is genuinely beautiful.

blocks.orig: If you want to learn more about Tanzania during your trip to the country, we would recommend adding a trip to Bagamoyo to your itinerary.
blocks.html: Anyone keen to understand the country's past a little better would do well to make room for Bagamoyo on their itinerary.

blocks.orig: You will also be able to find out lots of information about the slave trade that occurred in Bagamoyo during your trip, as this is the location from which slaves were shipped to Zanzibar.
blocks.html: During your visit you can also learn a great deal about the slave trade that took place in Bagamoyo, as this is the place from which slaves were shipped to Zanzibar.

blocks.orig: Another peaceful and tranquil place to visit is Kikuletwa Hotsprings. These hot springs are located along Arusha and Moshi, and they are essentially a jungle oasis.
blocks.html: Kikuletwa Hotsprings is another calm and tranquil spot. The springs lie along Arusha and Moshi and are essentially an oasis in the jungle.

blocks.orig: The Kikuletwa hot springs are a beautiful turquoise color, so they are perfect for any Instagram posts. They are also perfect for swimming, relaxing, and being at one with nature.
blocks.html: The water here has a lovely turquoise shade, ideal for your Instagram feed. It is equally good for swimming, unwinding and simply enjoying the natural surroundings.

blocks.orig: This really is a hidden gem that not many people speak about.
blocks.html: This is a real hidden gem that few people talk about.

blocks.orig: Finally we would recommend a visit to Mwanza and Lake Victoria. Lake Victoria spans across multiple African countries, and it is a very popular destination for tourists.
blocks.html: Lastly, we would suggest visiting Mwanza and Lake Victoria. The lake stretches across several African countries and is a very popular tourist destination.

blocks.orig: However, the banks of Lake Victoria in Tanzania are some of the most sparsely visited, so why not take advantage of this?
blocks.html: The Tanzanian shores of Lake Victoria, however, are among the least visited, so why not make the most of that?

blocks.orig: It is the same lake that you will see in Kenya and Uganda, it is simply less busy, so why not enjoy the peace and explore Mwanza while you’re there during your trip?
blocks.html: It is the very same lake you would see in Kenya and Uganda, only much quieter. So why not enjoy the calm and explore Mwanza while you are there?

blocks.orig: In short, in this guide, we have taken a look at 20 of the best tourist attractions in Tanzania. So if you are planning a luxury vacation, you should consider fitting these into your trip.
blocks.html: To sum up, this guide has covered 20 of the best tourist attractions in Tanzania. If a luxury holiday is on the cards, these are well worth building into your trip.
